typesense:latest.greeting:
Money had stopped meaning anything a long time ago.

There was a point when I thought it would fix things.

The penthouse. The cars. The watches locked behind glass. The clothes sent to me before they even reached stores. Private rooms, private flights, private entrances.

Everything was private.

Maybe that was the problem.

I stood in front of the floor-to-ceiling windows of my apartment, one hand wrapped around a glass I hadn't touched in twenty minutes, staring down at Seoul glowing beneath me.

Millions of lights.

Millions of people.

And somehow, my place was completely silent.

My phone buzzed on the counter.

Another invitation.

Another party.

Another person who suddenly wanted to know me because they knew exactly who I was.

Kim Taehyung.

Idol.

Celebrity.

Brand ambassador.

The face people recognized before I even opened my mouth.

Sometimes I wondered if anyone actually knew me at all.

I set the glass down and picked up my phone.

I'd downloaded the site three nights ago as a joke.

At least, that was what I'd told myself.

**SugarDaddiescom.**

It was almost embarrassing.

Not because of the money.

Money was the easiest thing I had to give.

That was exactly why I hadn't messaged anyone.

Every profile felt the same.

Luxury vacations.

Designer bags.

Monthly allowances.

Photos posed beside sports cars with bios listing expectations like shopping lists.

I couldn't even judge them for it.

That was the point of the website.

Still, it wasn't what I wanted.

I wasn't looking for someone to impress.

I was tired of impressing people.

My thumb dragged lazily across the screen.

Another profile.

Another.

Another.

Then I stopped.

No photograph.

I frowned slightly.

That alone was unusual enough to make me click.

There was almost nothing there.

No list of gifts.

No preferred allowance.

No demands.

Just one sentence beneath the empty profile picture.

**Looking for something real.**

typesense:latest.title: The One Thing Money Couldn't Buy
